summary: Konami racing line beginning with the 1984 overhead arcade racer Road Fighter and continuing through pseudo-3D and card-linked arcade sequels.

entries.title: Road Fighter

emulation.notes: Use the arcade version for the primary route; Arcade Archives is the clean legal modern route when available.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade-accurate emulation with modern display scaling

primary.why: Road Fighter began as a 1984 Konami arcade game before MSX, Famicom/NES, mobile, compilation, and Arcade Archives routes. The arcade original has the full six-stage format and is the reference version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version through Arcade Archives on PlayStation 4/Nintendo Switch if owned, or in MAME/original hardware; use MSX/NES only for historical port comparison.

entries.title: Midnight Run: Road Fighter 2

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation or hardware for primary; PlayStation emulation is the fallback.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade route where supported, otherwise high-resolution PlayStation emulation

primary.why: Midnight Run: Road Fighter 2 is the 3D arcade sequel to Road Fighter and later received a PlayStation version in Japan and Europe. The arcade release supports the original cabinet-style multiplayer route and is the reference version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME if supported or on original hardware; use the PlayStation version only as a home fallback.

all_releases.fidelity: Original arcade release with linked multiplayer support.
all_releases.reason: primary: original cabinet route and highest-authenticity version.

all_releases.fidelity: Home PlayStation conversion released in Japan and Europe.
all_releases.reason: skip: home route and no sourced content advantage over arcade.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: The European PlayStation release is titled Midnight Run, removing the Road Fighter connection.

entries.title: Winding Heat

emulation.notes: Use original arcade hardware or arcade emulation where compatible.

primary.why: Winding Heat is the arcade-only sequel to Road Fighter and Midnight Run, moving the racing to touge-style roads and offering linked cabinet play. No home version is sourced.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or through MAME if support is available.

all_releases.fidelity: Original arcade release with linked cabinet configurations.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced home port or remaster.

entries.title: Road Fighters

emulation.notes: Emulation/preservation may not reproduce all network and card-linked features.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original arcade cabinet including stereoscopic display where available

primary.why: Road Fighters is a Japan-only 2010 arcade sequel with stereoscopic 3D hardware, licensed cars, real-location tracks, and card-linked tuning/customization. It has no sourced home release.
primary.how_to_play: Play on surviving original arcade hardware; preservation access depends on arcade board and network feature availability.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Japanese arcade release with stereoscopic display hardware and card-linked features.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Single sourced platform route, but online/card features are part of the original arcade design.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home port; e-Amusement service was disconnected from 2015.
